text:
raj: Heads-up — after we flipped the new egress gateway for the dedicated GPU pools in ap-southeast, about half the edge nodes are getting DNS timeouts. Affected: staging + a couple prod zones.

molly: Can you paste a failing `dig` and the node's /etc/resolv.conf? Also which NAT/GW did we flip?

raj: Here's a quick `dig` from an affected node:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @127.0.0.53 internal-service.prod.redwood
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
And `/etc/resolv.conf` is pointing at systemd stub: `nameserver 127.0.0.53` with `options edns0 single-request`
We flipped to the new regional NAT64 pool (egress-gw-aps-2) earlier this morning.

michael: Huh. Could be EDNS / fragmentation or UDP blackholing on the path. Can you run a `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53` while reproducing? Also check `ss -u -a` to see socket queues.

raj: tcpdump shows lots of outgoing DNS queries to our upstreams but no replies coming back for many of them. When replies arrive they sometimes have TC=1 (truncated) but node-local-dns doesn't seem to retry on TCP quickly.

molly: Two quick hypotheses: 1) The new NAT/GW is dropping or mangling UDP responses (maybe DF/fragmentation/IPv6-to-IPv4 translation edge case with NAT64), and 2) our node-local-dns/systemd-resolved interaction is fragile when upstream switches IPs leading to short cache/TTL churn and increased queries.

kevin: Also check iptables conntrack. If conntrack table overflows or entries time out weirdly while DNS uses high port ephemeral source, replies could be unmatched. `conntrack -L | grep 53`

raj: Ran conntrack — a bunch of DNS entries in ESTABLISHED/RELATED but many show ASSURED=0 and short timeout. I pushed a small capture to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-debug/dns/1765439123.pcap

michael: Workaround idea: force node-local-dns to prefer TCP fallback for truncated responses and increase the resolver retry timeout temporarily. Also we can add a dedicated SNAT rule for traffic to our upstream DNS IPs that bypasses the new NAT64 pool so DNS stays on the old path.

molly: I inspected iptables rules around nat POSTROUTING — the egress-gw rule was masquerading *after* we had DNAT for node-local-dns redirection which caused source ports to change unexpectedly on the way back. Moving the MASQUERADE earlier and pinning upstream-dns IPs to a static SNAT should stop replies being dropped.

raj: I applied a targeted SNAT for the three upstream DNS IPs (old egress path) and bumped node-local-dns `--cache-ttl` to 5s -> 30s to reduce churn. Seeing resolution success rate jump to ~98% on the previously-affected nodes.

kevin: Can we make this a permanent guardrail? If the new egress pool causes any UDP fragging or conntrack mismatches, we should automatically pin DNS to a known-good egress and add an e2e test in the infra CI that opens 10k parallel DNS queries through new egress before flip.

molly: Agreed. Followups: 1) Add SNAT exceptions for upstream DNS on egress change runbook, 2) update node-local-dns config to enable faster TCP fallback and a slightly longer cache TTL by default, 3) add CI job to stress-test DNS over the egress pool.

deploy-bot: Scheduled runbook update task #ENGINFRA-442 to create SNAT exception template and CI test.

raj: Rolling patch looks stable. Will monitor for 30m and then remove temporary logging. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
